It has also been used for ultrarapid detoxification under anaesthesia, although a sys- tematic review3 concluded that the risks outweighed the ben- efits of using opioid antagonists in such procedures. A later study4 also failed to support the use of such a regimen. After detoxification, patients may be given oral naltrexone for maintenance; subcutaneous formulations of naltrexone have also been used in an attempt to improve compliance, although serious complications, including deaths, have been reported5-7 with their use. 1.
